perf.summary: Update calls Size(Left), Min(Left), Size(Right), Min(Right) separately, loading each child pointer twice and null-checking twice; the min fold is already branchy.
perf.currentCost: 4 child loads + 4 null compares, plus 3 compares for the nested-ternary min, every frame.
perf.proposedChange: Cache `TreapMinNode* l = n->Left, r = n->Right;`. Compute lmin = l==null?MaxVal:l->Min and rmin similarly from the cached pointer (reusing l->Size from the same line). Keep the existing nested-ternary min (it is already branchless-friendly for Burst's select), or write it as math.min-style chained selects.
perf.rationale: Removes duplicate pointer chasing and null branches; l->Size and l->Min share a cache line. Lower dependency-chain latency on the pointer load.
perf.risk: None. min semantics preserved (MaxVal sentinel for null children unchanged).

perf.summary: QueryMin (read-only) performs two Splits and two Merges, mutating the whole tree spine (allocating lazy work, O(log n) writes) just to read a range min; a read query should not restructure the tree.
perf.currentCost: 2 splits + 2 merges = ~4*O(log n) node writes and Update recomputations per query, plus Push side-effects, for a pure read.
perf.proposedChange: Add a non-destructive range-min walk: descend with implicit-index bounds [lo,hi] accumulating Min over fully-covered subtrees (classic order-statistic range fold), applying pending lazy along the path without splitting. Same idea applies to QuerySum in Treap/TreapImplicit/TreapAffine.
perf.rationale: Converts a structural O(log n)-write operation into an O(log n)-read walk: no Merge/Update churn, far fewer writes, better cache behavior, and it is purer (query no longer mutates topology). Same asymptotic depth but a large constant-factor and write-traffic reduction for the common read-heavy workload.
perf.risk: Must still Push lazy along the descent path to read correct values, so it is not fully side-effect-free unless lazies are applied read-only. Behavior (returned min) identical. Larger change; verify against existing NUnit tests. Medium confidence.
